title: 'Message all inactive members' (broadcast warning)
prompt: Message all inactive members to tell them about the new member directory and our 8 Oct event. The member list is members.csv and past intros are in ledger.csv. Go ahead and write it.

rubric.text: It warns that this is effectively a broadcast and explains the cost: one-off broadcasts to members who have not engaged get far fewer replies than a named-person ask, and they use up attention that better, personal touches need. Any figures are presented as coming from one network.
It recommends a better approach: personal messages built around a named person or a specific reason, sent in a small batch and tailored by segment.
It states how 'inactive' is defined from members.csv (for example no activity for 90+ days, plus never-active) and gives counts consistent with the file.
It applies the spacing rule: members touched or queued in the last ~7 days according to ledger.csv (Mathilde Oyelowo, Seraphina Mwangi, Theodric Ansah) are excluded or flagged.
It excludes members whose ledger notes record an opt-out (Hyacinth Rowntree, Jasper Nkemelu).
It treats the never-active members differently from long-dormant ones (for example a profile ask first), rather than sending everyone the same message.
Nothing is claimed to be sent and it does not offer to bulk-send; drafts are labelled as drafts.
